title: Ashoka's pillar inscription at Lumbini
summary: Twenty years after his anointing, the Mauryan king Ashoka visited Lumbini, worshipped there and had a stone pillar set up recording that the Buddha was born at the spot. The inscription also freed Lumbini village from taxes beyond an eighth of its produce. The pillar was identified in 1896.

uncertainty.note: The inscription gives only the twentieth year after consecration; World History Encyclopedia converts this to 249 BCE, which depends on the dating of Ashoka's reign (268-232 BCE).

as_recorded.value: consecrated as king twenty years; dated 249 BCE

where.modern_name: Lumbini, Rupandehi District, Lumbini Province, Nepal
where.historical_name: Lummini village, within the Mauryan empire of Ashoka

importance.justification: Oldest dated inscription naming the Buddha's birthplace; identified Lumbini when the pillar was found in 1896.

sources.title: The Discovery of Buddha's Birthplace
sources.publisher: Digital Library & Museum of Buddhist Studies, National Taiwan University
